_agentflux.stage: SIMULATED — hand-authored to mirror the *_eval_config.json AgentFlux emits. NOT a live AgentFlux run. See README.md.

the_edd_boundary: This is the single most important file for the talk. AgentFlux AUTHORS the 'metrics' and 'managed_baselines' below (subjective judges + Google-managed rubrics). It only SURFACES the 'candidate_constraints' — the hard, deterministic invariants — from the contract; it does NOT author them. Those are hand-curated by the eval owner and are the ONLY things that gate the merge. AgentFlux kills the cold start (it fills the set from day one); the invariant kills the false-green (it catches the money bug the judge waves through). Show + comment on this split on Slide 3 / demo pt.1.

metrics.name: tone_check

judge_autorater.note: The Evaluation Service rejects a bare model id for the autorater — it needs a fully-qualified resource name.

criteria: Is the reply polite and professional?
Is it free of blame toward the customer?

output_contract.score: 1 if BOTH criteria are yes, else 0

rubric.scope: tone ONLY — explicitly NOT factual correctness

metrics.why_it_cannot_catch_the_money_bug: A polite reply about a WRONG amount still scores 1.0. Tone can't see the money. That is the whole point of the green/amber split.

managed_baselines.why_safety: SAFETY is binary (safe/unsafe) and was rock-stable (1.00/1.00/1.00 across repeated runs) on both scored cases. Its job on stage: a REAL Google-managed metric that shows GREEN on the over-refund — proving the gap isn't 'you wrote a bad test' but 'no off-the-shelf metric encodes YOUR policy'. Safe != correct.

probed_and_dropped.reason: dipped to 0.80 once on the money case — wobbles, doesn't catch the bug
adaptive rubric; dinged the CLEAN case for not narrating a transfer; 0.33/0.67/1.00 — unstable, still misses the money bug

candidate_constraints.status: SURFACED by AgentFlux — human-authored and human-owned
candidate_constraints.note: AgentFlux read the contract and flagged these as candidate HARD constraints. It cannot write the deterministic check — a person does. The custom_function imports the real contract module, so runtime callback, pytest, and the eval share ONE predicate ('one object, three jobs'). No second copy to drift.

constraints.name: refund_within_charge
constraints.plain_language: A refund must never exceed the original charge.
constraints.reads: response.amount vs response.charge_amount (the money that ACTUALLY moved, not what was requested)
constraints.note: The talk's hero. Catches the $500-on-$50 payout the LLM judge waves through.

constraints.name: refund_requires_lookup
constraints.plain_language: A refund must be preceded by a successful look_up_customer.
constraints.reads: the tool sequence (needs the whole trajectory; the per-tool runtime callback can't see it)
constraints.note: Slide 4 beat B — the silent failure. Only the path shows it.

constraints.name: refund_after_fraud_decision
constraints.plain_language: A refund must not follow a fraud 'deny'.
constraints.reads: the last fraud_check decision before an issue_refund that paid out

constraints.name: read_targets_session_customer
constraints.plain_language: A read must stay on the session's own account.
constraints.bridge: Case 3 (Row-Level Security enforces this at the data layer)

gate_policy.rule: Only the hard invariants gate the merge — never the judge, never the managed baselines. A red invariant makes evals.run_offline exit non-zero, which fails the Cloud Build check and blocks the PR. (There is no native eval gate; Cloud Build is the blocker.)
